channel.title: Posts on MoscowMigrant
channel.description: Recent content in Posts on MoscowMigrant

item.title: Trump got offended
item.description: It seems that Putin overestimated his influence on Trump, who has clearly gone out of control. According to a global survey, there is not a single country in the world whose citizens consider Russia a main ally, and the majority perceive the Russian Federation as a threat.

item.title: Elite fall
item.description: Lately, Russian generals, top managers, and oligarchs have been experiencing three types of misfortunes: arrests for corruption, sudden deaths/suicides, and eliminations by Ukrainian special services.

item.title: Back to Stalin
item.description: The Communist Party of the Russian Federation declared Khrushchev's report on the cult of personality around Stalin to be erroneous. The BRICS resolution defended Russia and Iran, and condemned Ukraine, the USA, and Israel.

item.title: The sixth conversation
item.description: Putin explained to Trump that U.S. Independence Day is thanks to Russia. Russia was the first in the world to recognize the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan under Taliban leadership and banned the Norwegian Helsinki Committee.

item.title: Trump's betrayal
item.description: The suspension of U.S. military aid opens the Ukrainian sky to the occupiers. Why is Trump betraying Ukraine? Russia – Azerbaijan: a chronicle of a spiraling conflict.

item.title: Putin held a political briefing for Macron
item.description: Persecution of Azerbaijanis continues in Russia. Macron spoke with Putin, and he explained everything to him. Trump has halted the delivery of anti-aircraft missiles to Ukraine that were promised by Biden.

item.title: Russia is diligently cultivating an enemy out of Azerbaijan
item.description: Trump lifted sanctions on Syria; this country will soon no longer be a state sponsor of terrorism. Russia is deepening the conflict with Azerbaijan. Russians have suddenly overfulfilled the plan for developing civil identity.

item.title: The war may be entering a new phase
item.description: Trump has approved sanctions against Russia. The war may be entering a new phase. The Azerbaijan–Russia conflict has sharply escalated.

item.title: Khamenei and Trump are celebrating a victory, but it's unclear who they were fighting against
item.description: Khamenei and Trump are celebrating a victory, but it's unclear who they were fighting against. Orban is blocking Ukraine's accession to the EU, while Trump is demanding a pardon for Netanyahu and halting the investigation into Russia's crimes.

item.title: Ode to Trump, or Why Zelensky Wore a Suit
item.description: Трамп потребовал убить Голос Америки. Совет Европы создал трибунал по преступлениям России, который не сможет судить Путина. Марко Рубио отказался поддержать новые санкции против России. Саммит НАТО во славу Трампа, или зачем Зеленский надел костюм.

item.title: Everyone is celebrating the victory: the USA, Israel, and especially Iran
item.description: The results of the 12-day war: Iran is not giving up on nuclear weapons, some killed generals have come back to life, and the IRGC is tightening the screws. At NATO, Zelensky was welcomed like family by everyone except Trump, Orbán, and Fico.

item.title: The apocalypse seems to be postponed. But that's not certain
item.description: Trump stated that the war is over and thanked Iran for the delicate strike on the military base. Iran continues to strike Israel.

item.title: US strike on Iran and its consequences
item.description: US strike on Iran, its consequences, and the reaction of the global press. Lukashenko has released Sergei Tikhanovsky, who looks like a prisoner of Auschwitz.

item.title: Putin has found a new ally to replace Iran
item.description: Trump's rubber deadline is a universal tool: it works both in the Middle East and in Ukraine. The alliance between Putin and Matroskin the Cat is a force. A soft one.

item.title: Trumpists are divided over the Iran issue
item.description: Trumpists are divided over the Iran issue, and Trump called Tucker Carlson crazy. At the St. Petersburg Economic Forum, they paraded the children and grandchildren of the elite, as well as the Taliban.

item.title: World War III is taking on a protracted character
item.description: Trump-the-Empty-Bucket is saving Khamenei and Putin. Israel is unable to finish off Iran without U.S. support. The G7, without the U.S., failed to impose sanctions against Russia.

item.title: Khamenei must be eliminated
item.description: Today, global evil has taken the form of two specific individuals: Vladimir Putin and Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. No one has the political will to deal with Putin. As for Khamenei, Israel does have the political will—it's important that Trump doesn't interfere.

item.title: The Iran-Israel War and Trump the Peacemaker
item.description: Why Ali Khamenei, Like Putin, Got Lucky with the 47th U.S. President, and What Prevents Israel from Eliminating Iran's Nuclear Program.

item.title: Israel has launched an attack on Iran. This is the first stage
item.description: Israel has begun eliminating Iran's nuclear threat. Nuclear facilities and missile bases have been destroyed. The head of the IRGC has been killed. Trump stated that this will ruin everything.

item.title: The day of Russia's disgrace
item.description: Russia marked its day with strikes on Ukraine. A summit in Odesa and Vučić's demarche. Lev Shlosberg received a final warning.

item.title: Ukrainian resilience against the Russian military machine
item.description: KIIS poll: Ukrainians are ready to endure and are not ready to surrender. NATO Secretary General Rutte: Russia produces more ammunition than all NATO countries combined, and does so much faster.

item.title: California against Trump
item.description: California against Trump. Canada – is it Europe? Orban's revelations. The political striptease of self-proclaimed leaders of the Russian opposition.

item.title: The shadows of the past have gathered to speak about the future
item.description: The Tsargrad Institute is holding the Forum of the Future. Under the leadership of Dugin and Malofeev, prominent futurists such as Archpriest Andrey Tkachev, Ekaterina Andreeva, Pyotr Tolstoy, Sergey Mironov, and others are gathering.

item.title: How Elon Errolovich and Donald Fredovich had a falling out
item.description: Trump and Musk had a major falling out, and as a result, both became poorer. Trump decided to let Russia and Ukraine fight a little more and then punish them both severely.

item.title: Putin tattled on Ukraine to Trump, and Trump was deeply affected
item.description: Putin complained to Trump that Ukrainian terrorists were disrupting negotiations, and Trump lost interest in Ukraine and started asking Putin for help with Iran.

item.title: The SBU continues to strike at Russia's prestige
item.description: Everything that must explode will certainly be blown up, said Medvedev. Agreed, replied Maliuk. Orban said that Ukrainians are criminals and that he has a conscience.

item.title: A performance requested by a single audience member
item.description: The second round of Istanbul negotiations did not bring us any closer to peace, but it did provide a chance to address humanitarian issues. Poland has chosen the nationalist and Trumpist Nawrocki, adding to the ranks of Eurosceptics.

item.title: Ukraine has shown its cards
item.description: Operation Web, its military, political, economic, and moral significance. The reaction of Russian Z-enthusiasts, ultra-patriots, and also woolly liberals.

item.title: Putin's main resource
item.description: Trump is battling the courts and losing Musk. Zelensky offers real negotiations, while Russia insists on trolling. What is Putin's main resource?

item.title: Dreams of a new Yalta and their danger
item.description: Trump gives Putin two more weeks and wants a new Yalta, Zelensky is ready for a trilateral meeting with Trump and Putin, Putin demands to eliminate the root cause, and Europe is preparing for war.

item.title: Trump the Almighty and his Terrible Things
item.description: Trump is scaring Putin with terrible things, Medvedev is scaring Trump with World War III, and Russia continues to receive money from all over the world to keep the war going.

item.title: Vladimir the Mad
item.description: Merz announced the lifting of range restrictions on missiles supplied to Ukraine, Trump stated that Putin had gone mad, and Peskov explained that Trump was experiencing emotional overload.

item.title: Creeping Munich
item.description: Massive strikes on Ukrainian cities will intensify amid Trump's surprise and Kellogg's demands to immediately stop.

item.title: Russia is demanding that Ukraine change its president
item.description: Putin's posturing: the creation of a security buffer zone and the demand for Ukraine to change its president. More of Trump's exploits: banning Harvard from educating foreigners and accusing the president of South Africa of white genocide.

item.title: Forward, to the Orthodox Taliban!
item.description: Justice Minister Chuichenko called the Decembrists foreign agents, his deputy Sviridenko explained that a foreign agent could be an alien, and the head of the Investigative Committee Bastrykin laughed at the slogan Russia will be free.

item.title: Voice of America is dead, but Liberty will live on for now
item.description: Trump destroyed USAID and Voice of America, while Radio Liberty is still alive. After Trump's lovebirds' tweeting with Putin, the EU imposed four sanction regimes against Russia.

item.title: They had a talk...
item.description: Another phone chirping session between Trump and Putin, fairy tales about peace, ceasefires, and other details of the cover-up operation.

item.title: Trumpists are suffering defeat in Eastern Europe
item.description: In Romania, liberal Dan decisively defeated Trumpist Simion, while in Poland, liberal Trzaskowski is slightly ahead of Trumpist Nawrocki. European leaders tried to explain something to Trump before his call with Putin.

item.title: Putin's luck
item.description: How did it happen that a dictator leading a country with 1.5% of the world's GDP once again managed to bend to his will countries that surpass Russia dozens of times in economic and military terms?

item.title: The fog dissipated, revealing emptiness
item.description: Medinsky is once again leading the delegation, and the delegation consists of second-tier officials. Putin is once again deceiving the US and Europe.

item.title: Negotiation fog
item.description: A day before the negotiations in Istanbul, the official list of participants, the agenda, the start time, and most importantly, the purpose remain unknown. Meanwhile, Putin is busy creating a patriotic theater.

item.title: Istanbul Dead End
item.description: Four reasons why the Istanbul road will not lead to peace.

item.title: There is a war in Ukraine, negotiations in Istanbul, so what's the problem?
item.description: Putin's nighttime statement: to resume direct negotiations with Ukraine on May 15 in Istanbul without a ceasefire. This was a response to the joint statement by Zelensky and European leaders on a ceasefire starting May 12.

item.title: Day of lies and hatred
item.description: An American citizen who criticizes Trump's policies has been elected Pope. Victory frenzy has begun: Moscow is under siege, the Allies of the anti-Hitler coalition didn't show up, and the light at the end of the tunnel is Xi Jinping.

item.title: An uneasy sky hangs over all of Russia
item.description: Xi Jinping, Maduro, Vučić, Miguel Díaz-Canel, and Lula da Silva arrived for the Victory Day frenzy celebration. A powerful Ukrainian drone attack on May 7 was followed by a calm night on May 8. Putin's ceasefire seems to be holding.

item.title: India - Pakistan: war or special operation?
item.description: India and Pakistan have exchanged missile strikes. Nuclear weapons have not been used so far.

item.title: The brain drain from the United States is becoming a reality
item.description: Trump is pushing scientists out of the U.S., while Europe, Canada, and China are welcoming them with open arms.

item.title: Stylistics of neo-fascism
item.description: Russia is on the list of the most unfree countries, while the U.S. media freedom rating is declining. Putin and Trump demonstrate a unified style – boorish. And this style is finding followers all over the world.

item.title: Trump says goodbye, but he doesn't leave
item.description: The U.S. has authorized the sale of $50 million worth of weapons to Ukraine (not billion, but million). The U.S. State Department stated that the U.S. will no longer act as a mediator in the negotiations, while Vance announced that America will continue peace talks over the next hundred days.

item.title: Deal
item.description: Ukraine and the United States signed an agreement on natural resources. It does not contain any Ukrainian debts. Tucker Carlson directly accused Zelensky's government of attempting to assassinate Trump.

item.title: How to see peace in Putin's eyes
item.description: Patrushev separated Odesa from Ukraine, Medvedev called for the denazification of Europe, Putin named the Volgograd airport Stalingrad, and Trump saw in Putin's eyes a desire for peace.

item.title: One Hundred Days That Shook the World
item.description: Putin declared a victory-obsessed ceasefire. Canada voted against Trump in the parliamentary elections. Trump's first 100 days were the worst result in the past 80 years.

item.title: What is born from the current chaos
item.description: Trump suspected that Putin was messing with his head and said that he had a deadline, but did not specify what it was; Lavrov explained that haste hinders real politics, and Shmyhal stated that Ukraine owes nothing to the U.S.

item.title: Putin won the London battle with Trump's hands
item.description: After the collapse of the London summit, the US and Russia no longer hide their partnership: Trump reproaches Putin in a friendly manner, Lavrov showers Trump with compliments, and Naryshkin comes to the defense of the US president.

item.title: London dead end
item.description: Breakdown of negotiations in London and the remote exchange between Trump and Zelensky. Putin's bloody arguments. On the discussion between Kasparov and Podrabinek.

item.title: What can be seen through the London fog
item.description: Negotiations in London: Rubio and Witkoff are not going, the Kremlin denies Putin's ceasefire proposal, Zelensky opposes Trump's plan. What is the point of the negotiations?

item.title: Trump makes Ukraine an indecent proposal
item.description: Pope Francis – an epilogue. The U.S. makes Ukraine an indecent proposal, after which Witkoff will go to Putin to discuss the division of the world.

item.title: The Easter truce is over, forget it
item.description: The results of the special operation Easter Truce: Ukraine and Russia accused each other of violations. Putin will not extend the truce. The end of the negotiation farce is approaching.

item.title: Life inside a caricature
item.description: Putin thanked Hamas for its humanitarianism. Trump found out that Zelensky, it turns out, didn't start the war. Naryshkin's agency identified Hitler in the face of Ursula von der Leyen.

item.title: The closure of America
item.description: The consequences for the U.S. of anti-immigration orders, tourist detentions, and Trump's rudeness. Time magazine's list of the 100 most influential people in the world – what's wrong with it.

item.title: Trump banned the West from condemning Putin
item.description: Trump listens to Whitcoff, not Rubio, and forbids the West from criticizing Putin. Russian journalists were imprisoned for their honesty and professionalism. The Russian army is almost entirely dependent on supplies from North Korea.

item.title: Three-time hero
item.description: Trump found out that Biden and Zelensky are to blame for the war in Ukraine—well, Putin is also to blame. In Ukraine, they decided to hold a May 9 meeting with the heads of state of the anti-Putin coalition as a counterbalance to Moscow’s victory-frenzy.

item.title: The Kremlin is negotiating in the language of war crimes
item.description: After Whitkoff's meeting with Dmitriev – the tragedy in Kryvyi Rih, after Putin's negotiations with Whitkoff – the mass killing in Sumy.

item.title: Trump's swings against the backdrop of war
item.description: Negotiations through the eyes of Trump, Ukraine, and Russia. Who profited from Trump's swings. Greenland: a guide to annexation.

item.title: Trump-style pedagogy: China, get out of the classroom!
item.description: ТTrump decided to punish China for its disrespect, while putting everyone else on hold. The coalition of the willing and the meeting in the Ramstein format may formalize the split between Europe and the U.S.

item.title: The peace offensive... on the Sumy and Kharkiv regions
item.description: Under the cover of negotiations, Russia is preparing a new offensive. The CDU/CSU-SPD coalition will increase support for Ukraine. Trump declared that all countries kiss his ass, while China and Canada proposed the reverse procedure.

item.title: Who in Europe and the USA will raise the banner of the anti-Trumpist uprising?
item.description: Trump has challenged the entire world. So far, only China has picked up the gauntlet. Who will be able to accept this challenge in Europe and in the USA itself?

item.title: Negotiations within chaos
item.description: Elon Musk opposed Trump on tariffs, Marco Rubio opposed Putin on the ceasefire, Scott Bessent opposed Zelensky on the mineral deal.

item.title: World war. So far, it's just a trade one
item.description: Why did Putin’s fixer Dmitriev come to the US? Where did the myth of the US being robbed come from? How to silence America without any jammers.

item.title: Sulky person
item.description: Trump declared a trade war on the entire world and called it America's Liberation Day. It turned out that for the past half-century, the U.S. had been robbed, offended, and exploited. Most of all by Lesotho, Cambodia, Madagascar, and the penguins from uninhabited islands.

item.title: The Brown International and How to Fight It
item.description: War is a mother to some. How not to become cannon fodder. Why The Economist is lying about the elections in Ukraine in July. The battle for Le Pen as the rallying point for all the brown forces on the planet.

item.title: Unlimited deadline
item.description: Trump set a psychological deadline for Putin but forgot to name the date. Perhaps this is a know-how of combining the principle of a deadline with the practice of procrastination.

item.title: Trump threatens everyone with problems, but everyone just tells him to get lost
item.description: Trump is angry with Putin and is threatening Zelensky with serious trouble. Journalism and war: a highly timely article in the NYT and the awarding of an international prize to a TASS photographer.

item.title: Shura Burtin’s Journalism on Russia’s War in Ukraine: Themes, Tone, and Bias
item.description: A comprehensive review of Shura Burtin’s body of journalistic work, focusing on recurring themes, political framing, and his portrayals of Ukraine and Russia.

item.title: Putin: First we'll finish them off, then we'll talk
item.description: Putin explained that he would first finish off Ukraine, then place it under external control, and only after that begin negotiations. The debate between Zhdanov and Katz showed that Putin can rely on them.

item.title: Mitrofanushkas in the White House
item.description: U.S. President's special envoy Richard Grenell stated that the nuclear weapons Ukraine gave to Russia under the Budapest Memorandum were Russian. Trump continues Signalgate, blaming everything on the journalist.

item.title: Signalgate
item.description: The White House's new sincerity: the U.S. leadership invited a journalist into a closed chat where military plans were discussed. Following the talks in Riyadh, Moscow remains silent, Washington is talking, and Kyiv is outraged.

item.title: Let sleeping dogs lie
item.description: Can lies become the foundation of the world in Ukraine? This is not a rhetorical question in light of the recent statements by the U.S. State Department.

item.title: Putin - Trump: a love with benefits
item.description: Putin gave Trump a priceless portrait of Trump painted by Safronov, while Trump's friend Witkoff and Tucker Carlson spent an hour and a half lying non-stop about Ukraine, the war, and Putin.

item.title: Shuttle diplomacy carried out by the FSB
item.description: On Monday, indirect (shuttle) negotiations will take place between Russia and Ukraine, involving Ukraine's fierce enemies. The collapse of Tesla as a prelude to the collapse of the United States.

item.title: Putin suggested that Trump divide the world into three parts
item.description: Trump suggested that Zelensky give the U.S. nuclear power plants, while Putin proposed that Trump divide the planet into three with Xi. Erdogan is eliminating a political rival.

item.title: Five reasons why Trump's mission is impossible
item.description: The prosecutor demanded 18 years for dissident Skobov. Trump spoke with Putin on the phone. They agreed to continue negotiations and, in the meantime, play hockey. Five reasons why Trump's mission is impossible.

item.title: What is the danger of using historical arguments in politics
item.description: Trump strengthens the ruble, prepares to recognize Crimea as Russian, and declares Biden's pardons invalid. What is historical gratitude, and what is the danger of using historical arguments in current politics.

item.title: Why does modern America need the Statue of Liberty
item.description: Trump silenced the Voice of America and declared war on the Houthis. The French are demanding that the U.S. return the Statue of Liberty. Trump promised to talk to Putin on Tuesday about the distribution of certain assets.

item.title: Putin's Nuances
item.description: Putin thanked Trump and effectively refused a ceasefire. Why is the Middle East envoy negotiating with Russia? Trump continues to infringe on the sovereignty of Canada and Greenland.

item.title: Five questions about the truce
item.description: Dictator Duterte, a Putin sympathizer, will stand trial at the ICC. Putin is pausing in response to truce proposals, but the very idea raises at least five questions.

item.title: The ball is in Putin's court
item.description: The U.S. and Ukraine are offering Russia a 30-day ceasefire. The U.S. is resuming aid to Ukraine and continues to provide intelligence. How will Putin respond, and what will Trump do if Putin refuses?

item.title: To Ukraine – the whip, to Russia – the gingerbread
item.description: Before the meeting in Jeddah, Marco Rubio explained that if he liked its outcome, military aid would continue. Musk accused Ukraine of a cyberattack on the X network. USAID is no more – who suffered.

item.title: Trump team's debate style
item.description: Trump is called a deal-making maestro and a master negotiator. Here are some examples of the new dialogue style from the U.S. president and his team.

item.title: Ordinary Trumpism
item.description: Musk explained that empathy is the enemy of civilization, Rubio knows that in Ukraine, the U.S. is fighting against Russia, with Ukraine merely as an intermediary, and Kellogg accused the Ukrainians of halting U.S. aid. Trump's team is removing Zelensky from the negotiation process and holding talks with his opponents.

item.title: The United States, in the fourth year of the war, opened a second front. Against Ukraine
item.description: The suspension of American aid and intelligence sharing is direct support for Putin and the death of Ukrainian citizens. A new carrot-and-stick policy: the stick for Zelensky, the carrot for Putin. American democracy is resisting Trump.

item.title: Zelensky agrees to peace; now it's just a matter of convincing Putin
item.description: After Zelensky's conciliatory letter to Trump, their conflict seems to be resolved. Now Trump has to engage with Putin, and Vance won’t be of any help here.

item.title: Trump is, in fact, on Putin's side in this war
item.description: Trump has suspended military aid to Ukraine—the aid that was provided by the previous Biden administration.

item.title: Europe is persuading the US not to split the West
item.description: The echo of the scandal in the Oval Office. Europe has agreed on four steps to support Ukraine and has tried to persuade the US not to split Euro-Atlantic unity. Thanks to Musk, the US may get dozens of Snowdens.

item.title: The battle in the Oval Office and its consequences
item.description: Zelensky did not kiss the villain's hand but fought back against two fascist boors.

item.title: Russian protest without Nemtsov and Navalny
item.description: Before Zelensky's visit to the U.S., Trump found out that the President of Ukraine is, in fact, not a dictator. Tomorrow, a march of the Russian opposition is planned in Berlin.

item.title: Rare-earth scam
item.description: Why the rare-earth elements deal lacks economic substance, and who needs it and why.

item.title: Putin laid open the depths of Russia to Trump
item.description: The U.S. and Ukraine may strike a deal on rare earth elements. In response, Putin laid open the depths of Russia to Trump, and Trump peeked in with interest.

item.title: How to End the War
item.description: How to End the War

item.title: The alliance between the USA and Russia against Ukraine
item.description: Behind the votes on UN resolutions regarding the war in Ukraine, a new alliance between the USA and Russia against Ukraine is emerging. Trump explained that Zelensky is a dictator, while Putin is not, and Putin decided to lure Trump with rare earth elements.

item.title: Three years of hell
item.description: Three years later. Bundestag elections – preliminary results. How the Pentagon congratulated Trump by lying.

item.title: It's no longer Trump, but the U.S., and not against Zelensky, but against Ukraine
item.description: The U.S. urged the G7 not to call Russia an aggressor, halted arms sales to Ukraine, and is pushing through a deal on minerals. It's no longer Trump, but the U.S., and not against Zelensky, but against Ukraine.

item.title: Trump has started a war to destroy Zelensky
item.description: Trump called Zelensky a dictator without elections, a comedian with modest success, and accused him of derailing a deal on rare earth metals. This is already a war for political destruction.

item.title: Igor Yakovenko: Putin's Koschei's Needle is Located in Crimea
item.description: Transcript of Igor Yakovenko's YouTube broadcast in cycle 7-40
